channel.title: Cyber Threat Wall — New KEVs
channel.description: Vulnerabilities newly appearing in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

item.title: CVE-2026-53266 — Linux Kernel
item.description: Threat Signal 67. Linux Kernel contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the ebtables SNAT target which allows an ARP sender hardware address rewrite to write directly into a nonlinear socket-buffer fragment backed by a splice-imported file page. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

item.title: CVE-2025-39682 — Linux Kernel
item.description: Threat Signal 63. Linux Kernel contains an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions vulnerability in the TLS receive path which allows a zero-length record retrieved from the rx_list to bypass the intended recvmsg() record-type handling, potentially causing subsequent TLS records to be processed using incorrect zero-copy and queuing assumptions. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

item.title: CVE-2025-39964 — Linux Kernel
item.description: Threat Signal 60. Linux Kernel contains a race condition vulnerability which allows concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket causing data to be unpredictably interleaved and creating inconsistencies in the socket's internal state.
